what: Brookfield Renewable owns one of the world's largest portfolios of renewable power: hydroelectric dams, wind and solar farms, and storage, across the Americas, Europe and Asia. It is managed by Brookfield and structured as a partnership.
customers: Utilities, large corporations buying clean power under long-term agreements, and wholesale electricity markets.
money: long-life dams with low operating costs
onshore and offshore wind and solar farms
rooftop solar, storage and sustainable solutions
moat: Hydroelectric assets that cannot be rebuilt and last a century, plus a development pipeline and contracts with technology companies buying clean power for data centres.
risks: Consolidated debt of about $42 billion, though most is non-recourse at the asset level
It reported a net loss because of depreciation and minority interests
Rising interest rates raise the cost of funding new projects
It is a partnership, which complicates tax reporting for some investors
opportunities: Revenue grew about 9% last year and about 11% a year over three years
Technology companies signing long-term clean power agreements for data centres
A distribution yield above 5% with a record of annual increases
watch: Funds from operations per unit and new power purchase agreements signed.
